counterevidence_limits: Essay-format review by one author; 'central' is a disciplinary judgement.

wording: Homeostatic regulation involves multiple interacting feedback systems and feedforward control, not a single negative-feedback cycle.

counterevidence_limits: Pedagogical model; some systems may lack an explicit set-point representation.

wording: Allostasis (Sterling) argues that the primary goal of regulation is anticipatory adjustment, not constancy, and that feedback error-correction is inherently inefficient; this competes with homeostasis-centred accounts (S01) that include feedforward within homeostasis.
counterevidence_limits: Disagreement is partly terminological; neither source tests the other.

wording: In SIM-R1-C0 (toy loop), PI control restored the set point after a step load (tail mean 0.001), P-only left the analytic residual 0.476, degraded gains raised peak deviation (1.79 vs 0.36) and slowed recovery (10.99 vs 4.49), and a load beyond effector capacity was not corrected.

In SIM-R1-C0, adding anticipatory (feedforward) control cut the peak deviation from 0.360 to 0.086, while feedforward alone with a 20% estimation error left a residual of 1.987 — in this linear toy, anticipation and feedback are complementary.
counterevidence_limits: Does not decide the homeostasis–allostasis dispute (C0v2-R1-11).
